rachel: Quick blocker - optkit migration PR (#4910) failed linkcheck and sample coverage. Need tiny runnable snippets (batching + kv_prefetch + quant_profile) and a short migration checklist.

amit: I can add examples. Proposal: Python + Rust minimal recipe, plus 2-line rationale under each. Keep < 25 lines.

jorge: Also fix the quant profiles link - remove old internal URL and point to /optimize/quant-profiles#profile-table. And note the config rename `kv_prefetch.max_tokens` -> `kv_prefetch.max_prefetch_tokens`.

amit: Draft Python snippet (minimal):
```python
from redwood import Client
cli = Client(api_key="${REDWOOD_KEY}")
res = cli.generate(
  model="redwood-optimized-7b",
  prompt="Summarize in one line.",
  batching={"enabled": True, "max_batch_ms": 10},
  kv_prefetch={"enabled": True, "max_prefetch_tokens": 128},
  quant_profile="latency-tier-1"
)
print(res.text)
```

amit: Rationale: small batch window keeps median latency low; modest prefetch reduces cold-token cost; tier-1 quant gives mild memory savings with negligible quality loss. Use stronger quant when throughput >> 2000 req/s.

amit: Rust snippet (pseudo-api, to be copy-paste friendly):
```rust
let client = redwood::Client::new(env!("REDWOOD_KEY"));
let opts = redwood::GenerateOpts::builder()
  .model("redwood-optimized-7b")
  .batching(true, 10)
  .kv_prefetch(true, 128)
  .quant_profile("latency-tier-1")
  .build();
let resp = client.generate("Summarize in one line.", opts)?;
println!("{}", resp.text);
```

amit: Migration note (short): rename `kv_prefetch.max_tokens` -> `kv_prefetch.max_prefetch_tokens`. For backward compat, when old key present we map it to the new one in config parsing.
